verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const p="app/api/track/route.ts";if(!fs.existsSync(p)){console.error("SCAN-765: "+p+" missing");process.exit(79)}const s=fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8");const imp=/from\s+"@\/lib\/consent\/consent"|from\s+\x27@\/lib\/consent\/consent\x27/.test(s);const gate=/hasConsent\(\s*profile\.id\s*,\s*["\x27]analytics["\x27]\s*\)/.test(s);if(!imp||!gate){console.error("SCAN-765: /api/track writes an account-tied engagement_events row without checking the analytics consent scope, so a member who turned off Product analytics still has every nav.page_view stored against their profile (its sibling /api/observe honours the same toggle).");process.exit(1)}'

append.detail: app/api/track/route.ts resolved the member's profile and called track() with no consent check, so a member who turned off Product analytics still had every nav.page_view written to engagement_events keyed to their profile_id, while the sibling /api/observe dropped its batch on the same toggle. The route now imports hasConsent from @/lib/consent/consent, returns 204 when there is no profile, returns 204 without calling track() when hasConsent(profile.id, 'analytics') is false (ADR-069, the /api/observe gate), and passes profile.id to track(). lib/analytics/track.ts is unchanged so server-authoritative events still feed the ledger. Pinned by app/api/track/route.test.ts (consent off: 204 and track never called; no profile: 204; consenting: recorded under the profile id; non-client event still 400). docs/ANALYTICS.md notes that /api/track is consent-gated.
